questions.question_text: In the balanced equation 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, what does the coefficient 2 before H₂ indicate?
questions.option_a: Two molecules (or moles) of hydrogen react per one molecule (or mole) of oxygen
questions.option_b: Each hydrogen molecule contains two oxygen atoms
questions.option_c: The reaction produces two atoms total
questions.option_d: The mass of hydrogen is twice the mass of oxygen
questions.explanation: Coefficients give relative numbers of reacting molecules or moles; they do not directly give relative masses.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Chemical Reactions and Equations, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, what mass of ammonia can form from 6 g of hydrogen when nitrogen is in excess?
questions.explanation: Six grams H₂ is 3 mol; the stoichiometric ratio gives 2 mol NH₃, whose mass is 2 × 17 = 34 g.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A student weighs reactants in an open flask, carries out a reaction that releases carbon dioxide, and then weighs the flask contents. The measured mass falls mainly because
questions.option_a: some gaseous product escaped from the open system
questions.option_b: mass was destroyed during bond formation
questions.option_d: the balance changed the atomic masses
questions.explanation: The conservation of mass applies to a closed system; an escaping gas causes an apparent mass decrease in an open vessel.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Chemical Reactions and Equations, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which equation is balanced for the reaction of hydrogen with chlorine to form hydrogen chloride?
questions.explanation: Two hydrogen atoms and two chlorine atoms occur on both sides in H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Chemical Reactions and Equations, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: When silver chloride is exposed to sunlight, it decomposes to silver and chlorine. Which condition drives this decomposition?
questions.explanation: Silver chloride is photosensitive and undergoes photochemical decomposition, a reaction used in traditional photographic processes.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Chemical Reactions and Equations, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A black solid of silver oxide is heated and forms shiny silver with oxygen gas. Which reaction type best describes the chemical change?
questions.explanation: Heating one compound to produce simpler substances is thermal decomposition: 2Ag₂O → 4Ag + O₂.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: During electrolysis of water acidified with a small amount of electrolyte, which volume ratio of hydrogen to oxygen is collected under comparable conditions?
questions.explanation: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂, so twice as many hydrogen molecules and volume as oxygen are produced under the same conditions.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Hydrogen gas is passed over heated copper(II) oxide. Reddish copper forms and water is produced. In this process, copper(II) oxide is
questions.explanation: CuO loses oxygen to form Cu, so it is reduced; hydrogen gains oxygen and is oxidised to water.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Chemical Reactions and Equations, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Chlorine gas is bubbled through potassium iodide solution and iodine appears. Which substance is reduced?
questions.explanation: Cl₂ gains electrons to form Cl⁻ and is reduced; iodide loses electrons to form iodine.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Chemical Reactions and Equations, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: During Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻, the iron ion undergoes which change?
questions.explanation: Fe²⁺ loses one electron as its oxidation state rises from +2 to +3, so it is oxidised.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A reaction transfers electrons from one reactant to another. Why must oxidation and reduction occur together?
questions.option_a: Electrons lost by one species must be gained by another
questions.option_c: Only oxygen atoms can accept electrons
questions.explanation: Electron transfer is conserved: oxidation releases electrons and reduction consumes them, so the processes are coupled in a redox reaction.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An aqueous solution of lead nitrate is mixed with potassium iodide. A bright yellow solid forms. The solid is
questions.explanation: Pb²⁺ and I⁻ ions form insoluble yellow PbI₂; KNO₃ remains dissolved in solution.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A solid reactant is crushed into much finer particles before a gas reacts with it. What is the usual effect?
questions.option_a: The reaction is faster because more solid surface is exposed
questions.option_b: The reaction stops because the solid loses all atoms
questions.option_c: The reaction becomes slower because there is more surface
questions.option_d: The equilibrium constant must increase at every temperature
questions.explanation: For a heterogeneous reaction, finer particles expose more surface for contact and collisions, generally increasing reaction rate.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A catalyst speeds up a reaction but is not consumed overall. It does so mainly by
questions.option_a: providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy
questions.option_c: changing the equilibrium constant at fixed temperature
questions.option_d: making an endothermic reaction violate energy conservation
questions.explanation: A catalyst offers a pathway with lower activation energy and is regenerated; it does not change the equilibrium constant at a fixed temperature.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A reaction mixture becomes noticeably colder while the reaction proceeds. If the temperature change is due to the reaction absorbing heat from its surroundings, the reaction is
questions.explanation: An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from its surroundings, often causing the surroundings or mixture to cool.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which everyday process is an exothermic chemical reaction that releases energy stored in glucose?
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration oxidises glucose and releases usable energy; melting and evaporation are physical endothermic changes.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT science references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: When a copper strip is heated in air, a black coating forms. The coating is principally
questions.explanation: Copper reacts with oxygen on heating to form black CuO, a combination and oxidation reaction.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A packet of chips is flushed with nitrogen before sealing. The main purpose is to
questions.option_a: reduce oxidation of oils and delay rancidity
questions.explanation: Nitrogen displaces much of the oxygen in the package, slowing oxidative rancidity of fats and oils.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Chemical Reactions and Equations, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement about a reversible chemical reaction at equilibrium is correct?
questions.option_a: Forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates
questions.option_d: The amount of every substance must be equal
questions.explanation: At dynamic equilibrium, forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates; concentrations remain constant but need not be equal.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which change usually increases the rate of a chemical reaction by increasing the kinetic energy and collision frequency of reacting particles?
questions.explanation: Higher temperature generally increases particle kinetic energy and the fraction of collisions energetic enough to react.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The Haber process forms ammonia by N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃. Increasing pressure favours ammonia formation because the product side has
questions.option_c: the same number of gas molecules
questions.explanation: The reactant side has four moles of gas for every two moles on the product side, so higher pressure shifts equilibrium toward ammonia.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The equilibrium N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g) is endothermic in the forward direction. What happens to the brown colour when the mixture is warmed?
questions.option_a: It becomes darker as more brown NO₂ forms
questions.option_b: It disappears because all NO₂ freezes
questions.option_c: It remains exactly unchanged at equilibrium
questions.option_d: It turns blue because nitrogen is produced
questions.explanation: Heating favours the endothermic dissociation of colourless N₂O₄ into brown NO₂, deepening the colour at the new equilibrium.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Potassium chlorate decomposes on heating to potassium chloride and oxygen. Which gas test supports oxygen formation?
questions.option_c: A lighted splint gives a pop
questions.explanation: Oxygen supports combustion and can relight a glowing splint.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The reaction 2NO + O₂ → 2NO₂ converts colourless nitrogen monoxide into brown nitrogen dioxide. In this reaction, NO is
questions.explanation: Nitrogen in NO has oxidation state +2 and rises to +4 in NO₂, indicating oxidation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which change in a reversible reaction mixture can shift equilibrium without changing the equilibrium constant at a fixed temperature?
questions.option_d: Changing the atomic number of a reactant
questions.explanation: Concentration changes can shift the equilibrium position; the equilibrium constant changes with temperature, not with concentration.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: For A ⇌ B, the equilibrium constant Kc for the reverse reaction B ⇌ A is
questions.explanation: Reversing a reaction inverts its equilibrium constant: Kreverse = 1/Kforward.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: For an ideal gaseous equilibrium in a rigid container, adding an inert gas at constant volume usually does not shift equilibrium because
questions.option_a: the partial pressures of reacting gases remain unchanged
questions.option_b: the inert gas reacts with every product
questions.explanation: At fixed volume and temperature, adding inert gas does not change the reacting gases’ partial pressures or concentrations, so the equilibrium position is unchanged.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which quantity changes when the temperature of a chemical system changes, even if the concentrations are momentarily held fixed?
questions.option_a: The equilibrium constant for a temperature-sensitive reaction
questions.option_b: The atomic number of every element
questions.option_c: The number of protons in each molecule
questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant depends on temperature; concentration or pressure changes alone shift position but do not alter K at fixed temperature.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
